en: He himself was the healer's wish,
He understood the heart and let it be taken,
His eye had traveled through blood,
O, if Karach is a hero,
Asking what the night would become,
Share with the one who has seen sorrow,
Asking what the day would become,
Swiftly invoking the forefather,
May God be the cause of his throne,
Asking that he protect himself,
His marvel came from a sorrowful land,
Everything he had done was exhausted,
Saying he would see him alive,
Saying he would take clothing from the hollow,
Omur had wished for it,
Koruk had wished for it,
Making the mineral treasure clash,
From the Indian who did not know the language,
He swelled with what would follow,
The age of a bull, the number of a camel stallion,
He roared when he struggled,
He grew fiercely heated and shouted,
Its frame was a willow branch,
It was torn out by the roots,
He aired the felt in the place of honor,
Mounting him upon the coal-gray horse,
Manas became a river,
Leading many children onward,
Giving him the horse Akkula,
Quickly giving his white musket,
Sending him on toward Talas,
His wrestlers entered his service.
Giving red gold and jewels,
The champion who emerged overcame the warriors,
Such was Jeljetpes’s renown,
His weight was equal to a thousand men,
Often enraged, he surged forward,
He wrestled with lions,
He set the hawk upon its quarry,
He gathered a great army.
Noble one, believe and consider,
The entrusted livestock lay there,
Tethered there as the days passed,
Along the banks of the Masin River,
So great a multitude summered there.
Peaceful since the forefathers’ time,
Do not ask where the old man dwells,
When one looks, it cannot be caught by the eye,
Could it stand for so long?
Its contrary nature could not be known,
He truly halted and set things in order,
The true holy man became their guide,
Spreading out along the noble ridge,
They tethered what had been set aside,
The heroes entered with an uproar,
The heroes cried out together,
Seven heroes rode at a trot,
Jeljetpes and the Kulan-Saryk heroes,
The giant gray-maned heroes were splendid,
When they halted, all became peaceful,
Night had not yet vanished from their driven eyes,
It was a deed their forefather had never seen,
The heroes each took their proper place,
Countless men filled the ridge,
Then he held his nose,
Jeljetpes laid his burden of guilt to rest.
The leopard surged and whispered.
Clouds broke apart in the clear sky.
Driven by the wind, they changed shape.
Day and night the wind drove on.
Tongues were bound as misery rose.
The heroes endured their span of life.
Their livestock remained, and their heads were safe.
God ordained Tagasha’s course straight.
Between the two they came upon a pasture.
When he looked, they waited while driving the livestock.
They made their living and winnowed grain.
The place where they settled was here.
